title: Foraminifera are absent from coarse gravels because of hydraulic sorting by currents

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Foraminifera are absent from coarse gravels because of hydraulic sorting by currents

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Foraminiferal shells are absent from coarse sands and gravels not because they avoid concussion but because light shells are sorted by currents like any other graded sediment, settling where water is still.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XII: The Spiral Shells of the Foraminifera

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The coarseness or fineness of the sediment on the sea-bottom is a measure of the current: where the current is strong the larger stones are washed clean, where there is perfect stillness the finest mud settles down; and the light, fragile shells of the Foraminifera find their appropriate place, like every other graded sediment, in this spontaneous order of lixiviation.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XII, “The Spiral Shells of the Foraminifera”; topic “Strength as a supposed selective factor”. Scope: foraminiferal shells in marine sediments

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch12-13: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.76

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The competing mechanisms make distinguishable predictions using paired biological and sedimentological observations. Large public marine repositories contain the needed variables, though harmonization and taphonomic controls are necessary.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Model foraminiferal shell abundance across sediment grain-size and current-speed gradients, including transport and settling traits, and compare hydraulic-sorting predictions with habitat-avoidance models based on living assemblages. Matching dead-shell distributions but different live distributions would support sorting; absence from both after flow controls would support avoidance.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Dissolution and sampling gear also alter shell distributions.

Many assemblage datasets mix living and dead tests.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The variables Thompson names, test abundance and sediment grade, are published together in multiple open PANGAEA sets, including stained living counts that help separate behavior from transport. Those sets do not constitute a global survey of coarse gravels, and sieving practice biases the record toward mud. A small team can test the association now on the available seafloors, which is a real but geographically restricted resolution of a general sedimentological claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Regress living and dead foraminiferal abundance on sediment grain size across surface samples, treating grain size as the current-speed proxy Thompson uses. Hydraulic sorting is supported if dead tests track the fine fraction the way other light particles do, including where living animals are present in coarser patches; habitat avoidance is favored if stained living specimens are absent from gravels even when transport is accounted for.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Most open pairs of counts and grain size are regional shelves, estuaries, or single cores.

Foraminiferal protocols often discard the coarse fraction, so true gravels are under-sampled.
